prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map divides the downward-angled stairwell scene into bright near surfaces within arm's reach (~0.2–0.5 m)—including a horizontal overhanging ledge across the top and a metal railing, yellow spirit level, and the camera wearer's left hand and yellow-sleeved right arm at the bottom—contrasted against a dark void for the flight of stairs and wall ~2–4 m below. No other people are present, so there is no facing or gaze direction toward the camera wearer; the wearer's body remains out of view behind the camera while their left hand (bottom center-left) partially occludes the spirit level and sits ~0.1–0.2 m left of their right arm (bottom right). Across frames 1 to 4 the spatial layout is nearly static with the bottom-left railing shifting slightly further into view, whereas in frame 5 the wearer's right arm and right hand move closer and higher into the bottom-right foreground (~0.2–0.4 m) as the camera angles slightly right. This map makes it easy to distinguish the close white top overhang from the distant white stairwell wall below—which blend together in color in the RGB image—Vertical step geometry on the distant stairs is lost in uniform blackness, and the left hand and spirit level merge into a single bright contour.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, and 4, detecting only a single pink 'person' mask for the camera wearer's left hand at the bottom center in frame 3 and two tan/pink 'person' masks covering the left hand and right arm/hand at the bottom-right in frame 5, all within arm's reach at ~0.2–0.5 m. It provides no spatial layout for the overhanging ledge above or the stairs ~2–4 m below, and because only the wearer's own extremities appear at the lower border (~0.1–0.2 m apart), no other people, faces, or gaze directions are present. Across the 5 frames, the masks appear intermittently and only reflect the upward and inward movement of the wearer's right arm and right hand into the bottom-right foreground in frame 5, leaving an unsegmented cutout where the spirit level and metal bar occlude the hands. While the negative space between the masks in frame 5 helps trace the silhouette of the held spirit level and bar against the wearer's hands, the map is largely unreliable because it misses the hands and arm entirely in three frames, fails to label any tools or structural surfaces, and splits the wearer's left and right sides into two separate 'person' instances in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all 5 frames, rendering neither yellow body skeletons nor magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. Because no keypoints are detected, the map alone conveys no spatial information about the overhanging ledge ~0.3–0.5 m at the top, the stairs and wall ~2–4 m below, or whether anyone is facing or looking toward the camera wearer. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer's left hand holds a yellow spirit level at the bottom center-left (~0.2–0.4 m away) roughly 0.1–0.2 m left of their yellow-sleeved right arm across frames 1–4, and the right arm and hand rise further into the bottom-right foreground to grip the metal bar in frame 5, with the rest of the wearer's body occluded outside the frame. The pose map shows nothing that is hard to see in the RGB image and is completely unreliable here, failing to detect the closely cropped egocentric hands and arm at the bottom edge of the frame.
